messages:
Nina Patel: heads up — ran into a weird install + auth flow while onboarding a contractor. `curl -sSL https://install.redwood.ai | sh` put redwoodctl in /usr/bin, but our dotfiles expect $HOME/.local/bin. novice users got confused.
Sam Gomez: installer should respect XDG and HOME. we used to have a --dest flag. is that gone?
Nina Patel: installer accepts INSTALL_DIR but not documented in quickstart. also the script auto-runs `redwoodctl login` at the end which starts a browser; on remote ssh sessions that hangs.
Owen Kline: yeah, remote ssh is the classic. suggest defaulting to printing post-install instructions and skipping the auto-login unless --auto-login passed.
Nina Patel: another auth weirdness: after browser flow completes, some users see `error: credential helper exit status 1` and no creds listed in `redwoodctl config list`.
Sam Gomez: repro'd this on Ubuntu 22.04. The helper writes to libsecret but the session daemon wasn't available in minimal cloud images. helper returned success to the CLI before secret was committed.
Owen Kline: we need a blocking flag or a poll inside the helper. small patch idea: retry the commit for up to 2s before returning success. also surface a clearer message: "credential store unavailable; try --store=file"
infra-bot: NOTE: new CLI v0.10.2 (canary) includes --store=file and improves installer docs.
Nina Patel: good. one more: `redwoodctl local serve --profile=onboard --config=./serve.yaml` ignored the profile when the config file specified profile: default. precedence seems backwards.
Sam Gomez: we merged a change earlier that made config file override CLI flags — that was unintentional. will revert. Until then, `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=onboard redwoodctl local serve ...` is the workaround.
Owen Kline: for onboarding doc I'll add examples: non-sudo install to $HOME/.local/bin, `redwoodctl login --device-code`, `redwoodctl login --store=file --file-path=~/.config/redwoodctl/creds.json`, and mention setting REDWOODCTL_PROFILE env var for serve.
Nina Patel: thanks — can someone add a note about tmux/ssh headless flows? new hires kept opening a browser on their laptop while trying to auth inside a cloud VM.
Sam Gomez: will add. filing two GH issues: installer-ssh-autologin (#441) and credential-helper-blocking (#442).
Nina Patel: awesome. Leaving a quick snippet for the onboarding doc:
```
# non-sudo local install
curl -fsSL https://install.redwood.ai | sh -s -- --install-dir "$HOME/.local/bin"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# headless login
redwoodctl login --device-code --profile=onboard --store=file --file-path="$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/creds.json"

# verify before starting local serve
redwoodctl auth status --profile=onboard || sleep 1 && redwoodctl local serve --profile=onboard
```
Owen Kline: nice snippet. :thumbsup:
